sections.h2: How can a Ramapo owner sell without the usual delays?
sections.html:
Work out which of Ramapo's overlapping governments bills and permits your house, settle the tax and certificate questions early, and choose a buyer who can close without a lender timeline. In Ramapo that first step matters more than in most towns, because the town contains a dozen incorporated villages and several unincorporated hamlets, and each village collects its own taxes.

Ramapo is a town in Rockland County with 61.14 square miles of land, bordering New Jersey to the south and Orange County to the west. The Census Bureau estimates 161,564 residents in mid-2025, up 8.5% from the 2020 base. By the 2020 count it was the most populous town in the state outside Long Island.

sections.h2: Which communities make up the Town of Ramapo?
sections.html:
The town is a patchwork. The villages inside it are Airmont, Chestnut Ridge, Hillburn, Kaser, Montebello, New Hempstead, New Square, Pomona, Sloatsburg, Spring Valley, Suffern and Wesley Hills. Monsey, Viola, Hillcrest, Tallman and Sterlington are hamlets, not villages.

Geography explains the pattern. The Ramapo River cuts a gap through the Ramapo Mountains at Suffern, and that pass carries the New York State Thruway, Interstate 287, State Route 17 and a rail line. State Route 59 runs from Nyack through Spring Valley to Suffern, and the Palisades Interstate Parkway touches the northeast corner. Torne Mountain in Harriman State Park overlooks the pass, and tradition holds that Washington watched the British fleet from its summit in 1777.

  • The western part of town is served by the Suffern Central School District.
  • The eastern part, including Spring Valley, Monsey, Pomona, Chestnut Ridge and New Hempstead, is served by the East Ramapo Central School District.
  • Rockland Community College is in the Viola area, about four miles east of Suffern.

The district on your parcel decides which school tax bill a buyer inherits, so name it correctly in the listing and on the disclosure form.

sections.html:
The town's typical owned home is valued at $653,100, and the average household has nearly four people. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page supplies the figures below, with 2020 to 2024 survey estimates unless noted.

With 3.84 people per household and nearly four in ten residents under 18, space is in demand, and additions and converted basements are common reasons a certificate of occupancy question comes up. The building section below covers it.

sections.h2: Who collects tax in Ramapo, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
The Town of Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes collects school and property taxes for about 30,000 parcels, but not for the villages. The town's own FAQ is explicit: each village bills and collects separately, so a house in Airmont or Suffern has a village bill that the town does not handle.

  • County and town tax can be paid in four installments for a 5% service charge. The first goes to the Town by January 31, and installments 2 through 4 go to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance.
  • School tax cannot be split. The Receiver says partial payments are not accepted on the school bill.
  • The penalty period starts in October for school taxes and in February for county and town taxes.
  • A missing bill does not excuse a late payment under Real Property Tax Law section 922.

The Receiver's advice to sellers is direct: skip the installment plan if you are about to sell. The plan adds 5% of the bill, and it can create confusion at the closing, where the seller receives credit for the unused part of the taxes. Call the tax office at (845) 357-5100 for a payoff or a tax history, and ask your closing attorney to check village bills separately. When a mortgage is paid off, the Receiver also asks owners to send the satisfaction letter to both the town and village tax offices so future bills reach the right address.

sections.h2: What does the Ramapo Building Department do before a sale?
sections.html:
The Building, Planning and Zoning Department reviews building permits and works with the Planning Board and the Zoning Board of Appeals. The Building Department says its aim is to make the permit and certificate of occupancy process as simple as possible, and its page lists forms that sellers of unusual properties may need.

  • Required Inspections for One- and Two-Family Dwellings, which shows the inspection steps a permitted project must pass.
  • A Certificate of Use application.
  • A Secondary Dwelling application, for a second unit on the property.
  • A Plumbing Test Certification form.

The town also runs an online Property Search tool. Use it, and the permit application package, to compare what the town has on file with what is actually built. If you converted a basement, added a kitchen or built an addition, confirm a certificate of occupancy exists. A buyer's attorney will ask, and the state's disclosure form asks the seller the same question.

sections.h2: What does a Ramapo seller pay to transfer the deed?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Rockland County Clerk with the TP-584 transfer tax return and the RP-5217 transfer report. Ask the clerk for current recording fees, since the county sets them, and ask your closing attorney when the TP-584 is due.

State transfer tax runs $2 for every $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500, and the seller usually pays it. A $653,100 sale is taxed as $653,500, which is 1,307 units of $500 and a tax of $2,614. A residential sale of $1 million or more adds a 1% mansion tax on the buyer.

On the disclosure side, the seller of a one to four family home must sign the statement and deliver it before the buyer signs a binding contract. If you later learn something that makes it inaccurate, a revised statement is due as soon as practicable, but not after title transfers or the buyer moves in, whichever comes first.

faqs.q: Does the Town of Ramapo collect my village taxes?
faqs.a: No. The town's own FAQ says each village bills and collects its taxes separately, so a house in a village has a village bill in addition to the town, county and school bills.

faqs.q: Should I use Ramapo's installment plan if I am selling?
faqs.a: No. The Receiver of Taxes advises against it, because the plan adds a 5% charge and can cause problems at closing, where the seller gets credit for the unused portion.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Ramapo house?
faqs.a: The western part of town, including Suffern, Montebello, Airmont, Sloatsburg and Hillburn, is mainly in the Suffern Central School District, and the eastern part is in the East Ramapo Central School District.

faqs.q: How is transfer tax figured on a Ramapo sale?
faqs.a: At $2 per $500 of the price, rounded up. A $653,100 sale rounds to $653,500 and owes $2,614.

faqs.q: How do I find out whether my Ramapo house has a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: Start with the town's Building Department and its Property Search tool, then confirm with the department by phone at (845) 357-5100.
